source_text: τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς οἰκονομίαν· Ὡς πρόβατον γὰρ ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθην καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἔναντι τοῦ κείροντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος. Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐφεδρεύει μοι ὁ διάβολος, ἁρπάσαι μου τὴν σάρκα ὡς πρόβατον θέλων, δεδιὼς δὲ ὡς ποιμένα τὴν θεότητα ὑπαναχωρεῖ καὶ φεύγει, διὰ τοῦτο κρύπτω μου ὡς ποιμένα τὴν θεότητα, προΐεμαι δὲ τὴν σάρκα ὡς πρόβατον, ἵνα θαρρήσας προσέλθῃ, προσελθὼν δὲ ἁρπάσῃ, ἁρπάσας δέ μου τὴν σάρκα ὡς πρόβατον ἀναιρεθῇ τῇ διστόμῳ μαχαίρᾳ τοῦ πνεύματος. Παῦσαι οὖν, αἱρετικέ, δειλίαν μου καὶ ἄγνοιαν καταψηφιζό μενος. ∆ειλιῶ γάρ, ἵνα δείξω ἀφαντασίαστον τῆς σαρκὸς τὴν ἀνάληψιν. Λέγω· Ἡ ψυχή μου τετάρακται, ἵνα μάθητε ὅτι οὐκ ἄψυχον ἀνείληφα σῶμα, ὡς ἡ Ἀπολλιναρίου βούλεται πλάνη. Μὴ τὰ πάθη οὖν τῆς σαρκὸς τῷ ἀπαθεῖ προσρίψῃς λόγῳ· θεὸς γάρ εἰμι καὶ ἄνθρωπος, αἱρετικέ. Θεὸς ὡς ἐγγυᾶται τὰ θαύματα, ἄνθρωπος ὡς μαρτυρεῖ τὰ παθήματα. Ἐπεὶ οὖν θεός εἰμι καὶ ἄνθρωπος, εἰπὲ τίς ἐστιν ὁ παθών; Εἰ ὁ θεὸς ἔπαθεν, εἶπες τὸ βλάσφημον· εἰ δὲ ἡ σὰρξ ἔπαθεν, τί τὸ πάθος προσάπτεις ᾧ τὴν δειλίαν οὐκ ἐπιρίπτεις; ἄλλου γὰρ πάσχοντος ἄλλος οὐ δειλιᾷ καὶ ἀνθρώπου σταυρουμένου θεὸς οὐ ταράττεται. Καὶ ὅτι ἡ σὰρξ ἔπαθεν, ἀπαθοῦς μείναντος τοῦ λόγου, μάρτυς Ἠσαΐας, ὃς ἐν πνεύματί με αἱμαγμένον θεασάμενος ἠρώτα· Ἵνα τί σου ἐρυθρὰ τὰ ἱμάτια; Τὰ ἱμάτιά σου, φησίν, ἐρυθρά, καὶ οὐχὶ σύ. Τὸ μὲν γὰρ σῶμα τιτρώσκεται, ὁ δὲ τῆς θεότητος οὐ παραβλάπτεται λόγος. Μάρτυς δὲ καὶ Ἰακὼβ ὁ πατριάρχης ὁ περὶ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Πλυνεῖ ἐν οἴνῳ τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς τὴν περιβολὴν αὐτοῦ. Ποίαν στολήν; τὸ σῶμα. Ποίῳ αἵματι; τῷ ἐκ τῆς πλευρᾶς ῥεύσαντι.
thought_title: The sheep and the shepherd: why Christ hides his divinity
orientation: Christ is still speaking in his own defense, explaining to the heretics why he displayed fear and human weakness before his passion.

Since therefore lies in wait against me the devil, to seize my flesh as a sheep wanting, but fearing as shepherd the divinity he withdraws and flees, because of this I hide my as shepherd divinity, I put forward but the flesh as a sheep, so that having taken courage he may approach, having approached but he may seize, having seized but my flesh as a sheep he may be destroyed by the two-edged sword of the spirit. Cease therefore, heretic, cowardice of me and ignorance condemning. I am cowardly for, so that I may show unphantasied of the flesh the taking up. I say: The soul of me has been troubled, so that you may learn that not soulless I took up a body, as the of Apollinaris wants error. choices.english: the plan of salvation of the flesh
choices.why: The glossary requires 'plan of salvation' for οἰκονομία; the genitive σαρκός is kept as 'of the flesh' to preserve the literal force.

choices.term: ὡς πρόβατον γὰρ ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθην
choices.english: For as a sheep to slaughter I was led
choices.why: The passive aorist ἤχθην is rendered 'I was led' to keep the passive voice and the sheep imagery from Isaiah 53:7.
rejected: I was brought as a sheep to the slaughter

choices.term: δεδιὼς δὲ ὡς ποιμένα τὴν θεότητα
choices.english: but fearing the divinity as a shepherd
choices.why: The participle δεδιὼς is causal, and the accusative τὴν θεότητα is the object of fearing; 'as a shepherd' preserves the ὡς phrase.
rejected: but being afraid of the divinity as of a shepherd

choices.english: the assumption of the flesh to be free from illusion
choices.why: ἀφαντασίαστον is a predicate adjective modifying ἀνάληψιν; the rendering keeps the adjective as a predicate and avoids the banned 'human nature' for σάρξ.
rejected: the unillusory assumption of the flesh
the non-phantasmal taking up of the flesh

choices.why: The dative τῷ ἀπαθεῖ λόγῳ is the indirect object of προσρίψῃς; 'impassible' is the standard theological term for ἀπαθής, and 'Word' follows the glossary for λόγος.
The phrase is ambiguous; 'in spirit' is kept literal for ἐν πνεύματι, and αἱμαγμένον is rendered 'bloodied' to match the Isaiah imagery of stained garments.
rejected: having seen me stained with blood in the Spirit

pass_b_english: the plan of salvation of the flesh. For as a sheep to slaughter I was led, and as a lamb before its shearer is silent (Isaiah 53:7). Since the devil lies in wait for me, wanting to seize my flesh as a sheep, but fearing the divinity as a shepherd he withdraws and flees, for this reason I hide my divinity as a shepherd and put forward my flesh as a sheep, so that he may take courage and approach, and approaching may seize it, and seizing my flesh as a sheep he may be destroyed by the two-edged sword of the Spirit. Stop, then, heretic, condemning me for fear and ignorance. For I am afraid so that I may show the assumption of the flesh to be no illusion. I say, 'My soul is troubled,' so that you may learn that I have not assumed a body without a soul, as the error of Apollinaris wants it. Do not, then, attach the passions of the flesh to the impassible Word. For I am God and man, heretic: God, as the miracles guarantee; man, as the sufferings testify. Since therefore I am God and man, tell me who it is who suffered. If God suffered, you have spoken blasphemy. But if the flesh suffered, why do you attach the passion to the one on whom you do not cast the fear? For when one suffers, another does not fear, and when a man is crucified, God is not troubled. And that the flesh suffered while the Word remained impassible, Isaiah is witness, who, seeing me bloodied in the Spirit, asked, 'Why are your garments red?' Your garments, he says, are red, and not you. For the body is wounded, but the Word of the divinity is not harmed. And Jacob the patriarch is witness, who says concerning me, 'He will wash his robe in wine and his wrap in the blood of the grape' (Genesis 49:11). What robe? The body. What blood? That which flowed from the side.

problems.quote: who seeing me bloodied in spirit asked
problems.source_quote: ὃς ἐν πνεύματί με αἱμαγμένον θεασάμενος ἠρώτα
problems.why: ἐν πνεύματί means 'in the Spirit' (prophetic inspiration), not 'in spirit' (mental state). Isaiah saw by the Spirit, not Christ was 'bloodied in spirit.' The English misattributes the prepositional phrase.
problems.fix: who, seeing me bloodied in the Spirit, asked
problems.ruling: ἐν πνεύματί modifies θεασάμενος ('seeing in the Spirit'), not αἱμαγμένον; 'bloodied in spirit' misattributes the phrase.

edits.old: who seeing me bloodied in spirit asked
edits.new: who, seeing me bloodied in the Spirit, asked

fixed: Changed 'in spirit' to 'in the Spirit' because the source's ἐν πνεύματί refers to prophetic inspiration, not Christ's mental state.

problems.quote: I am afraid so that I may show the assumption of the flesh to be free from illusion
problems.source_quote: δειλιῶ γάρ, ἵνα δείξω ἀφαντασίαστον τῆς σαρκὸς τὴν ἀνάληψιν
problems.why: ἀφαντασίαστον means 'not imaginary' or 'real, genuine' (showing the incarnation was not a phantom), not 'free from illusion'.
problems.fix: For I fear so that I may show the assumption of the flesh to be no illusion.

last_rejected.why: Source has 'for this reason' (διὰ τοῦτο) linking back to devil's fear; English drops the causal connector.
last_rejected.fix: for this reason I hide my divinity as a shepherd and put forward my flesh as a sheep
last_rejected.ruling: English 'for this reason' appears earlier; 'so that' captures purpose. Not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: the assumption of the flesh to be no illusion
last_rejected.why: ἀφαντασίαστον means 'not a phantom/apparition' (i.e., real), not 'no illusion' — the point is the assumption is not imaginary.
last_rejected.fix: the assumption of the flesh to be no phantom
last_rejected.ruling: 'No illusion' and 'not a phantom' are equivalent in meaning; both deny unreality.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ὡς πρόβατον γὰρ ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθην καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἔναντι τοῦ κείροντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος
last_rejected.why: The source quotes Isaiah 53:7 but the English marks it as Isaiah; however, the source lacks explicit attribution, so adding it is an addition. More critically, the source's next quotation from Isaiah lacks verse reference in English.
last_rejected.fix: Remove '(Isaiah 53:7)' or verify if source contains it; add '(Isaiah 63:1-3)' or similar for the garments passage.
last_rejected.ruling: Source verbatim quotes Isaiah 53:7 LXX; adding reference is standard scholarly annotation, not a meaning-changing error.

last_rejected.quote: seeing me bloodied in the Spirit
last_rejected.why: 'In the Spirit' means prophetically, not 'bloodied in the Spirit' as location; Isaiah saw by the Spirit.

last_rejected.ruling: ἐν πνεύματί με αἱμαγμένον θεασάμενος: 'seeing me bloodied in the Spirit' is acceptable; ἐν πνεύματι can denote visionary context.
